#!/bin/bash
# build one C# file the way the lessons do (the image's restored project), but keep
# the build's own output (timing lines) off the page unless the build fails
set -e
rm -rf /tmp/cs && cp -r /opt/templates/csharp /tmp/cs && cp "$1" /tmp/cs/Program.cs
cd /tmp/cs
dotnet build --no-restore -v q -nologo -clp:NoSummary > /tmp/cs-build.log 2>&1 || { cat /tmp/cs-build.log; exit 1; }
dotnet bin/Debug/net10.0/Program.dll

Cy is 0
JsonException: JSON deserialization for type 'RequiredPerson' was missing required properties including: 'age'.

gotcha.title: A field is missing from the JSON
gotcha.looks_fine: Loading `{ "fullName": "Cy" }` raises no error in Go, Python, TypeScript or C# (the tabs show what each one does with the missing `age`).
gotcha.rust_sees: The struct says `age: u32`: always a number. The JSON has no age, so serde returns an error that names the field instead of making a value up.
gotcha.why: A plain `int` field cannot tell a real 0 from a missing value afterwards. In Rust you say what you mean: `Option<u32>` if it may be missing, or `#[serde(default)]` if 0 is a fine answer. Other languages can ask for the same strictness (the C# tab shows `required`); in serde it is what you get when you write nothing.

fixed.name: examples/optional.rs
fixed.out: Cy didn't tell us their age

go.says: Go fills in the zero value, so `Age` is 0 and `err` is nil. Nothing in the result says the field was missing, and a real 0 would look the same.

python.says: `json.loads` does not know about a shape: you get a dict without an `"age"` key and no error at load. The dict is faithful to the text, but code that expects an age finds out only when it reads `cy["age"]`, and then it is a `KeyError`.
python.code:
import json

cy = json.loads('{ "fullName": "Cy" }')  # no "age"
print(cy)
try:
    print(cy["age"])
except KeyError as e:
    print("KeyError:", e)

typescript.says: `JSON.parse` returns whatever is in the text, and `as Person` only tells the compiler to believe you. The type says `number`, the value is `undefined`, and `undefined + 1` is `NaN`.

csharp.says: `System.Text.Json` leaves `Age` at its default, 0, with no error. Marking the properties `required` makes it throw, as the second line of the output shows.

kotlin.says: Not run here: the image has no kotlinx.serialization runtime. Its documentation says an object can be deserialized only when all its properties are present in the input, and that a property with a default value is optional.
